changelog: - **Lead source attribution, and a Source name unique per org** (#2570, story #2568). `Source.name` was a global `@unique`, so a second tenant creating "Google Ads" got a 409 about a row it could not see; it is now `@@unique([orgId, name])` (a composite over a column that was already unique cannot produce duplicates, so `db push --accept-data-loss` applies it on a populated table — verified locally with rows in both the NULL and a stamped org; `check:schema-push` prints its generic warning). No org-prefixed names. Every Source create goes through `findOrCreateSource()` (`src/lib/leadSource.ts`) with an explicit `orgId` — `/api/sources` and `/api/admin/sources` created rows with none, which is why #2542 had to leave source lookups unscoped — and reads the tenant (legacy NULL rows included) before inserting, so the default org cannot create a twin that would break the NULL → default backfill. Every source read is narrowed with `tenantWhere`/`withinTenant`: both source lists, the `[id]` DELETE (another tenant's source is now a 404, it used to be deleted by id), `/api/admin/source-users`, the source checks in `/api/mentor/mentees` and `PATCH /api/users/[id]`, and both halves of `/api/admin/analytics/sources`, whose `unsourced` count was platform-wide. A default-org source can carry another tenant's leads (the pre-#2570 pickers were unscoped), so the per-source lead count on `/admin/sources` is narrowed to the tenant as well, and the report counts a lead whose source lies outside its tenant as unsourced instead of losing it; `prisma/check-tenant-misattribution.mjs` gained a `source` signal that sizes those rows. The mapping is pure and unit-tested (`src/lib/leadSourceName.ts`, `scripts/test/lead-source-name.test.mjs`): affiliate reference > utm_source > acquisition_source > unknown, named `affiliate:<code>`, `utm:<source>/<medium>/<campaign>` (lower-cased, `-` for a missing part) and `channel:<value>`; unknown creates no Source and is counted in the report's explicit `unsourced` bucket. The marketing demo form's conversion (#2569) binds its lead through it; the marketing import and the hand-typed lead bind their `source` column to the org's Source of that name (first touch — an existing lead with a referrer keeps it, and no Source is created for it). The name is planned by the diff from the incoming column (`MarketingFunnelPlan.sourceName`), not from `leadChanges`, which omits a `referralSource` the lead already carries — so re-importing a book whose leads predate attribution binds them (the row reports `lead.source`), and a second run is UNCHANGED again. `sourceIdForLead()` is the entry point the SaleVali ingest (#2450) will call. MARKETING reads the report on `/admin/analytics` (#2421's decision, unchanged); `/admin/sources` stays on the `sourcing` capability.

en: Leads from the website demo form, the account import and the manual lead form are now attributed to a source automatically — the campaign they came from, or the source you typed — so the source report on the analytics page counts them. Leads with no known source are listed separately.
Two organisations can now each have a source with the same name, such as "Google Ads".
tr: Web sitesindeki demo formundan, hesap içe aktarımından ve elle girilen lead formundan gelen lead'ler artık otomatik olarak bir kaynağa bağlanıyor — geldikleri kampanyaya ya da yazdığınız kaynağa — ve analitik sayfasındaki kaynak raporu onları sayıyor. Kaynağı bilinmeyen lead'ler ayrıca gösteriliyor.
İki organizasyon artık aynı adlı bir kaynağa, örneğin "Google Ads"e, ayrı ayrı sahip olabiliyor.
de: Leads aus dem Demo-Formular der Website, dem Konto-Import und dem manuellen Lead-Formular werden jetzt automatisch einer Quelle zugeordnet — der Kampagne, über die sie kamen, oder der Quelle, die Sie eingetragen haben — und der Quellenbericht auf der Analyseseite zählt sie. Leads ohne bekannte Quelle werden gesondert ausgewiesen.
Zwei Organisationen können jetzt jeweils eine Quelle mit demselben Namen haben, etwa „Google Ads“.
